source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 6 (book p. 272); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Three things to handle: a factor 2, two different inverse functions, and an answer in \(\cos^{-1}\).
Plan: remove the 2 with the double formula, change both terms into \(\cos^{-1}\), then use formula (iii).
steps:
Given: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) and \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}\).
To prove: their sum is \(\cos^{-1}\frac{36}{85}\).
Method: (1) \(2\tan^{-1}x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\) turns \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4}\) into one \(\tan^{-1}\); (2) write both angles as \(\cos^{-1}\); (3) add with formula (iii).

Remove the factor 2
\[2\tan^{-1}\tfrac{1}{4}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{2 \cdot \frac{1}{4}}{1 - \frac{1}{16}}\]
\[= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1/2}{15/16} = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{8}{15}\]
Why: the double formula holds for \(-1 < x < 1\), and \(x = \frac{1}{4}\). \(\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{15}{16} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{16}{15} = \frac{8}{15}\).

Change \(\sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) into \(\cos^{-1}\)
\[\alpha = \sin^{-1}\tfrac{3}{5}\]
\[\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{9}{25}} = \tfrac{4}{5}\]
\[\alpha = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{4}{5}\]
Why: \(\alpha\) is in the first quadrant, so its cosine is positive (triangle 3, 4, 5).

Change \(\tan^{-1}\frac{8}{15}\) into \(\cos^{-1}\)
\[\beta = \tan^{-1}\tfrac{8}{15}:\ \text{opposite } 8,\ \text{adjacent } 15\]
\[\text{hypotenuse} = \sqrt{8^{2} + 15^{2}} = 17\]
\[\cos\beta = \tfrac{15}{17},\quad \beta = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{15}{17}\]
Why: \(\tan\beta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\); Pythagoras gives the hypotenuse; \(\beta\) is in the first quadrant.

Apply formula (iii) with \(x = \frac{4}{5},\ y = \frac{15}{17}\)
\[\sqrt{1-x^{2}} = \tfrac{3}{5},\quad \sqrt{1-y^{2}} = \tfrac{8}{17}\]
\[\text{L.H.S} = \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{4}{5}\cdot\tfrac{15}{17} - \tfrac{3}{5}\cdot\tfrac{8}{17}\right)\]
\[= \cos^{-1}\left(\tfrac{60}{85} - \tfrac{24}{85}\right) = \cos^{-1}\tfrac{36}{85}\]
\[= \text{R.H.S}\]
Why: the roots are the sines \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\sin\beta = \frac{8}{17}\). \(5 \times 17 = 85\).

Check
\[\sin^{-1}0.6 + 2\tan^{-1}0.25 \approx 0.6435 + 0.4900\]
\[= 1.1335\]
\[\cos^{-1}\tfrac{36}{85} \approx 1.1335\ \checkmark\]
Why: a calculator in radian mode agrees.
